summary: Expose each Nex Core host's available libvirt/QEMU CPU models in the VM create and edit forms, and define named choices as exact custom CPU models with fallback forbidden.

guide.reason: The CPU model selector now includes the actual named models available on the selected host and both creation and edit guides explain their availability and migration constraint.

api.reason: Inventory adds cpu_models from Core's libvirt/QEMU. VMCPU.model accepts a validated named model; Core rechecks availability before define and uses custom/exact XML with fallback forbidden. Authentication, authorization, operations, replay and outage handling are unchanged.

state.reason: A selected CPU model is pool-scoped VM configuration; the availability list is a read-only Core observation.
state.record: The selected model remains in the full VM specification in the pool master's managed journal and returns through Inventory.managed.vms, so a fresh Controller re-adopts it. Inventory.cpu_models is discovered from the assigned Core host's libvirt/QEMU and is never Controller-owned state.

verification.method: 2026-09-10: focused protocol, Core XML, agent parsing and Controller validation tests passed. The simulated browser walkthrough passed against a real HTTPS Controller and simulated mTLS Core: a host-reported Skylake-Server choice appeared in the selector and the succeeded VM specification preserved it. npm run typecheck, npm run build, python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree, python3 scripts/generate_api.py --check and python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_api_contract.py passed. The browser run did not define a real libvirt domain; Core XML and availability checks are covered by Go tests.
